title: Practice 5: One direction, or round and about

blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.q: Я ___ (ходить — to go, walk, there and back or in general) на твой сайт.
exercises.why: **ходила** is the past tense (feminine) of **ходить** (to go, to walk) — the many-directions (or there-and-back) verb of its pair, with **идти** for one direction. past: он ходи́л · она ходи́ла · оно ходи́ло · они ходи́ли. — Wiktionary, «ходить» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Multidirectional verbs describe: 1. General motion, referring to ability or habitual motion, without reference to direction or destination; 2. Movement in various directions; 3. Repetition of completed trips; 4. In the past tense, a single completed round trip.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The present tense of all Russian verbs has a twofold function; it indicates: A. an action in progress ("actual" function); B. a repeated or habitual action ("repeated" function). However each action of going (to go on foot, to ride, to fly) is expressed in Russian by two parallel verbs: one for the function A — being on the way to … — иду, еду, лечу; another for the function B — usually, often, etc. to go to … (the motion to and from is understood) — хожу, езжу, летаю.» — DLI, Lesson 22.  «Ходить, ездить: these two verbs belong to the 2nd (И) type of conjugation. Notice that the consonant д changes into ж in the first person singular (like видеть — вижу — видишь).» — DLI, Lesson 22.  A past tense with no single goal in sight: repeated trips, or one completed round trip.  Compare: «Ребёнок ходит шесть месяцев.» (The child has been walking for six months.) — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0). «Птицы летают, рыбы плавают, а собаки ходят.» (Birds fly, fish swim, and dogs walk.) — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.q: Ты когда-нибудь ___ (летать — to fly, there and back or in general) на аэростате?
exercises.why: **летала** is the past tense (feminine) of **летать** (to fly) — the many-directions (or there-and-back) verb of its pair, with **лететь** for one direction. past: он лета́л · она лета́ла · оно лета́ло · они лета́ли. — Wiktionary, «летать» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Multidirectional verbs describe: 1. General motion, referring to ability or habitual motion, without reference to direction or destination; 2. Movement in various directions; 3. Repetition of completed trips; 4. Note. — Do not confuse the following: Самолёт летает над городом. (motion without a definite goal) — Самолёт летит над городом. (motion towards a definite goal) — both: The aircraft is flying over the city.» — DLI, Lesson 55.  A past tense with no single goal in sight: repeated trips, or one completed round trip. exercises.q: Несмотря на то, что на улице ___ (идти — to go, walk, one way) дождь, я выгулял свою собаку.
exercises.why: **шел** is the past tense (masculine) of **идти** (to go) — the one-direction verb of its pair, with **ходить** for many directions. past: он шёл · она шла́ · оно шло́ · они шли́. — Wiktionary, «идти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Unidirectional verbs describe motion in progress in one direction.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The basic meaning of the verbs идти, ехать, лететь is being actually on the way to some place: Мы идём в кино. Мы едем в город. Мы летим в Нью-Йорк. — right now.» — DLI, Lesson 20.  «The verb идти means "to go, be going". It refers to going on foot. This verb belongs to the 1st conjugation (characterized by the vowel -ё-, like живу, -ёшь, -ёт …).» — DLI, Lessons 19–20.  Compare: «Капитан идёт в штаб.» · «Он часто ходит в штаб.» — DLI, Lesson 22. «Мы идём в библиотеку.» (We are headed to the library.) — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.prompt: I took the dog for a walk even though it was raining.

exercises.q: Как олень ___ (лететь — to fly, one way)!
exercises.why: **летел** is the past tense (masculine) of **лететь** (to fly, to be flying) — the one-direction verb of its pair, with **летать** for many directions. past: он лете́л · она лете́ла · оно лете́ло · они лете́ли. — Wiktionary, «лететь» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Unidirectional verbs describe motion in progress in one direction.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The basic meaning of the verbs идти, ехать, лететь is being actually on the way to some place: Мы идём в кино. Мы едем в город. Мы летим в Нью-Йорк. — right now.» — DLI, Lesson 20.  «Лететь: this verb belongs to the 2nd (И) type of conjugation. Notice that т changes into ч in the first person singular.» — DLI, Lessons 19–20.  Compare: «Капитан летит в Вашингтон.» · «Он иногда летает в Вашингтон.» — DLI, Lesson 22. «Птицы летят на юг.» (The birds are flying south.) — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  ·  From Дмитрий Мамин-Сибиряк, «Золото».

exercises.q: ___ (идти — to go, walk, one way) к нему!
exercises.why: **идти** (the infinitive) (to go) — the one-direction verb of its pair, with **ходить** for many directions. — Wiktionary, «идти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Unidirectional verbs describe motion in progress in one direction.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The basic meaning of the verbs идти, ехать, лететь is being actually on the way to some place: Мы идём в кино. Мы едем в город. Мы летим в Нью-Йорк. — right now.» — DLI, Lesson 20.  «The verb идти means "to go, be going". It refers to going on foot. This verb belongs to the 1st conjugation (characterized by the vowel -ё-, like живу, -ёшь, -ёт …).» — DLI, Lessons 19–20.  Compare: «Капитан идёт в штаб.» · «Он часто ходит в штаб.» — DLI, Lesson 22. «Мы идём в библиотеку.» (We are headed to the library.) — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  ·  From Алексей К. Толстой, «Смерть Иоанна Грозного».
